source_note: Ide, Someya, Kawaguchi & Fujii, 'Strategic Multi-Agent Learning for Interpretable Action Valuation of All Players in Football', arXiv:2610.05961v1 [cs.LG], 5 Oct 2026 (Kenjiro Ide, Taiga Someya, Kohei Kawaguchi, Keisuke Fujii; Nagoya University / University of Tokyo / HKUST / RIKEN), 33 pages. MPE-inspired (Markov Perfect Equilibrium) action valuation for on-ball, off-ball, and defensive players in association football (soccer): each possession a finite-horizon dynamic game, each player an autonomous Markov agent (N=22 focal slots, not persistent identities). HONEST SCOPE: MPE is a motivating solution concept only — does NOT compute or verify an equilibrium strategy profile; continuation values bootstrapped from observed next actions (not best-response/greedy). EDMS (Expandable Decision-Making States, 74-dim: pressure/space/passing options/shooting/offside-line/possession context) vs PVS (92-dim positions+velocities). Q-value decomposed into successor-feature basis h (expected discounted sum of d=3 tactical features: shot value, possession-termination adjustment, attacking-third ball occupancy) + linear reward-weight theta=[1.0,-0.5,0.2] (heuristic, NOT estimated; future IRL). Two-stage estimation: linear semi-gradient TD initialization (Adusumilli-Eckardt dynamic discrete choice) -> MLP pretrain to reproduce (coefficients not transferred) -> AVI nonlinear refinement (observed-next-action Bellman targets, greedy only at inference). 15 role-masked actions (5 on-ball/1 defensive/9 off-ball). gamma=1 finite horizon (build-up unattenuated). Data: 95 J1 League matches 2023+2024 (Data Stadium), 25fps->10fps, 50 train/5 val/40 test, 10308 possessions/1561255 steps/42.81h. Results: independent RL collapses to forward movement in 99.21% off-ball states vs MPE most-frequent 17.63%; team Q vs season xG Spearman independent -0.37 vs MPE +0.29 (n=20, descriptive); EDMS lower TD MSE than PVS in both formulations (TD MSE NOT cross-comparable: scalar Q vs d=3 feature space). Post-hoc reweighting on fixed basis (attacking-third 0.2->1.0 flips backward-right->forward-right, no retrain). Qualitative: context-dependent off-ball (open-space/support/scoring) + preventive defensive space closure. Limitations: does NOT isolate MPE component (differs architecture/reward/objective/training; controlled ablation needed), does NOT verify MPE, manual weights, position-only state (no orientation/technical attributes), weak xG correlation, J1-only. Extracted faithfully (not a derivative summary). Equations 1-18 printed in math font that extracts garbled; reconstructed in labeled LaTeX and flagged here and in assumptions. Domain football matches catalog (association football / soccer multi-agent reinforcement learning; J1 League). Directly isomorphic to GSE's strategic-interdependence multi-agent kernel, interpretable successor-feature value decomposition, tactical state representation, post-hoc preference reweighting, role-relative focal-slot conditioning, and preventive off-ball defensive credit. No sportsbook lines/spreads/totals/implied odds in source or lifted into GSE.

reasoning_traces.think: The retrocausal genealogy of this paper is the strategic-interdependence turn in football action valuation. Kenjiro Ide, Taiga Someya, Kohei Kawaguchi, and Keisuke Fujii, posting to arXiv in October 2026 as 2610.05961, argue that valuing player actions requires accounting for continuous strategic interactions among twenty-two players including off-ball movements and defensive positioning, and that existing reinforcement-learning valuation methods either aggregate decisions at the team level or estimate player values independently, leaving strategic interdependence insufficiently represented. The work sits in the lineage of expected goals, VAEP's action valuation by scoring-and-conceding probability changes, expected possession value and expected threat, Voronoi and velocity-aware space control, and the GVDEP defensive framework, while building directly on Nakahara's multi-agent reinforcement learning valuation, the authors' own Expandable Decision-Making States, and Adusumilli and Eckardt's temporal-difference estimation of dynamic discrete choice models. The recursive theory of mind is the Markov-perfect-equilibrium-inspired dynamic game and its interpretable value decomposition. Each possession is formulated as a finite-horizon stochastic game with twenty-two autonomous agents whose Markov policies depend only on the current state, because history-dependent subgame-perfect strategies are computationally impractical in football's large continuous state space; the MPE condition requires each player's strategy to be a mutual best response, but the authors are explicit that they use MPE only as a motivating solution concept and never compute or verify an equilibrium profile. The Q-value is decomposed into a successor-feature basis, the expected discounted accumulation of three tactical reward features — shot value, possession-termination adjustment, and attacking-third ball occupancy — and a linear reward-weight vector fixed heuristically at one, minus one-half, and one-fifth, separating the learned future-feature accumulation from the specification of tactical preferences. Cross-layer veto adjudication is the two-stage estimation and its honest evaluation discipline. A linear semi-gradient temporal-difference estimator initializes the successor-feature basis on observed transitions, a randomly initialized multilayer perceptron is pretrained to reproduce those linear estimates without transferring the coefficients, and approximate value iteration then refines the basis against Bellman targets built from observed next actions rather than greedy best-responses, with greedy actions derived only at post-training inference and never fed back into the targets. The evaluation respects three separate diagnostics: temporal-difference mean squared error measures within-formulation consistency only, because the independent baseline errs in scalar Q-space while the proposed method errs in three-dimensional successor-feature space; the off-ball action distribution diagnoses ranking collapse; and the team-level association with season expected goals is an exploratory descriptive check, not confirmatory external validity. The implementation invariants map directly onto GSE. The MPE-inspired multi-agent formulation is GSE's strategic-interdependence kernel that accounts for surrounding players through the observed game state; the successor-feature decomposition is GSE's interpretable value-basis separation of feature accumulation from tactical preferences; EDMS is GSE's tactically interpretable state representation encoding pressure, space, passing options, and possession context; the post-hoc reward reweighting on a fixed basis is GSE's tactical-priority sensitivity analysis; the focal-slot conditioning with a shared backbone is GSE's role-relative value estimation; and the preventive defensive valuation is GSE's off-ball space-denial credit for movements that close dangerous space without touching the ball. The empirical results make the context-sensitivity claim concrete and honest. With EDMS held fixed, the independent baseline assigns the highest value to forward movement in 99.21 percent of evaluated off-ball states, a trivial collapse, whereas the proposed formulation's most frequent direction accounts for only 17.63 percent, and the team-level Q-value association with season expected goals flips from a negative Spearman rho of minus zero point three seven for the baseline to a weakly positive zero point two nine for the proposed model across twenty matched teams. Qualitative cases show context-dependent valuation: forward runs into open space, support movements when a teammate already occupies the forward lane, scoring-opportunity positioning, and defensive space closure; and raising the attacking-third weight from one-fifth to one flips the highest-valued action from backward-right to forward-right without retraining. The caveats close the account with the scope limits that bound the claim. The authors are explicit that the comparison does not isolate the MPE-inspired component because the two approaches differ in architecture, reward representation, learning objective, and training procedure, so controlled ablations with a common backbone are required; the implementation does not solve or verify a mutually consistent equilibrium; the reward weights are manual rather than learned, with inverse reinforcement learning flagged as future work; the state relies on positions and velocities without body orientation or technical attributes; the expected-goals correlation remains weak; and evaluation is confined to ninety-five J1 League matches. The invariant for GSE is to adopt the MPE-inspired multi-agent value formulation, the successor-feature decomposition with post-hoc preference reweighting, the EDMS interpretable state, the two-stage linear-then-nonlinear estimation with observed-action bootstrapping, and the preventive defensive credit, while carrying the no-equilibrium-verification, the non-isolated-component, the manual-weight, and the single-league limitations as honest bounds on what the learned action values can claim. The implementation scale and architecture give the result its empirical weight. The corpus is ninety-five J1 League matches from the 2023 and 2024 seasons provided by Data Stadium Inc., resampled from twenty-five to ten frames per second, split chronologically into fifty training matches from 2023, five validation matches and forty test matches from 2024, yielding ten thousand three hundred eight possession sequences, one million five hundred sixty-one thousand two hundred fifty-five time steps, and forty-two point eight one hours of play, with sequences between thirty and three hundred steps and the attacking direction normalized left to right; the independent baseline uses a sixty-four-unit GRU while the proposed model uses a shared sixty-four and thirty-two-unit multilayer perceptron pooled across the twenty-two focal slots, with linear pretraining for one epoch and up to twenty approximate-value-iteration iterations reusing the previous parameters and decaying the learning rate by zero point three at iterations five, ten, and fifteen.

Kenjiro Ide, Taiga Someya, Kohei Kawaguchi, Keisuke Fujii (Nagoya/Tokyo/HKUST/RIKEN); arXiv:2610.05961v1 [cs.LG] 5 Oct 2026. Existing RL aggregates team-level or independent players, missing 22-player strategic interdependence (off-ball + defense). Eq2 MPE V_i^pi*(s)>=V_i^(pi_tilde,pi*_-i)(s) (mutual best response, motivating NOT verified). Eq3 V_i=E[sum gamma^{k-t} r_i|s], gamma=1 (finite T, build-up unattenuated). Eq4 r_i=z_i^T theta (z player-specific attackers/shared defenders). d=3 features: shot value (shooter v_t=EPV, defenders -1), possession termination (C_t=E_t·1{no shot}·1{x<L/6}, opponent EPV V(-x,y)), attacking-third occupancy (1{x>=L/6=17.5m}, L=105m); theta=[1.0,-0.5,0.2] heuristic NOT estimated. Eq8/9 Q_i=h_i^T theta, h_i=E[sum gamma^{k-t} z_i|s,a] successor features (others' actions via realized joint, no enumeration). Continuation bootstrapped observed next actions not best-response (MPE-inspired not MPE算法). Metrics: TD MSE within-formulation only (independent scalar Q vs MPE d=3 feature space NOT cross-comparable; independent PVS 6.69e-4/EDMS 4.51e-4, MPE PVS 1.12e-2/EDMS 1.09e-2; EDMS lower both); off-ball collapse independent forward 99.21% vs MPE most-frequent 17.63%; team Q vs season xG independent rho=-0.37 vs MPE +0.29 (n=20, descriptive not confirmatory). Limitations: NOT isolate MPE component (differs architecture/reward/objective/training, ablation needed), NOT solve/verify MPE, manual weights (future IRL), position-only state, weak xG, J1-only.
